sentences.text: Pessoa Digital, at pessoadigital.pt, is the digital scholarly edition titled "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", a digital edition of the editorial projects and publications of Fernando Pessoa.

What it edits, above all, are the handwritten notes, lists and plans with which Pessoa conceived his work, set beside the works he published in his lifetime so as to trace the development of his oeuvre between planning and publication.

The leesharks.com authorship census, which asks how authorship is made, named, distributed, attributed and sustained across persons, personas, collectives and machine participation, admits it as an aggregator and holds it as a direct case in its area of heteronymy, asking how an edition holds Pessoa's own plans for his work, the lists and notes in which the names were assigned their works, beside what he published.

The CCeH's project page names its editors as Ulrike Henny-Krahmer (University of Rostock), Pedro Sepúlveda (Lisbon) and Jorge Uribe (Medellín), and its participants as the Laboratório de Estudos Literários Avançados (ELAB) of the Universidade Nova de Lisboa and the CCeH, where Ulrike Henny was responsible for the edition; for its other participants it refers to the edition's own team page.

The University of Rostock's announcement of 2023 gives the founding partnership as the Institute of Literature and Tradition (IELT) at the New University of Lisbon and the Cologne Center for eHumanities at the University of Cologne, and the core team as led by Pedro Sepúlveda and Ulrike Henny-Krahmer, with Inês Rebelo do Carmo among the speakers of its lecture "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa: Projects and Publications".
The two accounts name the Lisbon partner differently, a laboratory, ELAB, on the CCeH's page and an institute, IELT, on Rostock's, and the census follows the CCeH's.

The edition is hosted by the DCH and supported by Portugal's Fundação para a Ciência e a Tecnologia (FCT); for 2023 it received funding from the infrastructure project NFDI Text+, to make it more sustainable organisationally and technically and to integrate it into the research data infrastructure of Text+.

The surname of one editor is printed three ways across the two cards: Sepúlveda on both pages, Sepülveda in Rostock's account of the core team, and Sepúlvedo in the author line of the paper the CCeH cites.

Its framework project, Estranhar Pessoa, has run since mid-2013 at its own address; the edition was begun in 2014, at the CCeH from 2014 to 2016 and ongoing since, its web presentation was first launched in 2017, and the cooperation was extended to EAFIT University in Medellín, from 2019 by Rostock's account, represented by Jorge Uribe.

A workshop and public lectures at Rostock on 3 and 4 July 2023, organised by the Akademie-Juniorprofessur Digital Humanities, presented its development and sustainability measures, with an evening lecture by Sepúlveda and Uribe Lozada on "Disjecta membra and restitution in Fernando Pessoa's self-publishing".
The announcement gives Pessoa's dates as 1883–1935, where the CCeH's page gives 1888–1935 and English Wikipedia his birth on 13 June 1888.

The edition contains text transcriptions in TEI, facsimiles, indexes of persons, journals and titles, and visualisations of its data as timelines and a network of persons, and it is built on an eXist database with XQuery and XSLT scripts and JavaScript.
The CCeH gives as a representative publication "Networks of persons and figures in Fernando Pessoa's publication plans" (2018) and refers to the edition's own pages for the list of publications.

The census reads the edition as keeping the place where Pessoa's authorship was planned, a record of the names' works as Pessoa assigned them before publication fixed them, and sets that record beside #940's account of distinct named authorial functions.

Among the markers by which #940 tells a heteronym from a pseudonym is "A bounded corpus produced under the heteronym rather than attributed retroactively", and it holds that "A pseudonym changes the label attached to an authorial function. A heteronym changes the organization of the authorial function itself."
On the census's reading the plans hold the names' works as assigned before publication, the stage of the corpus that this marker concerns.

Pessoa's own typology, from his letter to Adolfo Casais Monteiro of 13 January 1935, distinguishes orthonym, heteronym and semi-heteronym, and Teresa Rita Lopes and later critics extended it with the proto-heteronym and the para-heteronym; on the archive's typology, collapsing these distinctions treats his practice as "elaborate pseudonym".

English Wikipedia gives Pessoa about seventy-five names besides his own and states that he called them heteronyms, a term he invented, and it links the edition from its article on him as "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa", with the words "and heteronyms".

The edition's network of persons and the 2018 paper on the persons and figures of the publication plans stand beside the archive's reading that Pessoa's distinctive contribution is the system of heteronyms, their reciprocal relations and the master-disciple structure.

#940's counter-principle holds that "The authorial function is attributable through the civil bearer without being reducible to that bearer": the civil bearer administers, publishes and answers for the work without becoming the exhaustive source of every authorial function operating through it, and the heteronymic architecture "ensures that the collapse registers as loss".

It sets "Ordinary editing, where the editor's contribution is supportive rather than function-constitutive" outside heteronymy, names "Pessoa's Caeiro, Reis, Campos, and the constellation of heteronyms around them" in the tradition it joins, and plans a deposit on the heteronymic operation in the Pessoa archive as ethical practice.

The archive's essay on the meta-heteronym names a heteronymic system whose personae produce, besides literary works, the institutional apparatus, introductions, criticism, historiography and bibliography, under which those works become legible, and reads Pessoa as the first modern meta-heteronym, incompletely.

It counts Sepúlveda, with Jerónimo Pizarro, Teresa Rita Lopes and Richard Zenith, in the material turn that moved Pessoa criticism from text to archive, to the trunk, the 25,000 pages, the fragments and the unexecuted projects, and holds that "Se o meta-heterônimo é uma tecnologia institucional, o arquivo é a sua materialidade".

It proposes that Pessoa's infrastructure, his editorial projects among it, be read as the meta-heteronymic operation in fragmentary execution, and gives as an instance the Tábua Bibliográfica of 1928, signed by the orthonym, which lists the heteronyms' works as works of independent authors.

It records the objection that most of the heteronymic prefaces stayed in the trunk, and states its own limit: the category is typological and provisional, and its validity depends on further tests in Pessoa's archive, above all in the unpublished materials of the Ficções do Interlúdio and the unexecuted editorial projects, the class of document whose plans and lists the edition holds.

#1722 holds that "A heteronym is a real author's practice: Pessoa wrote as Caeiro, Reis and Campos, and nobody concludes from this that Pessoa was a character", records a heteronymic practice, Pessoa's, read as a Sybil operation, answers that a heteronym is declared, its registry published with the orthonym, the roles and the dates, and counts the heteronymous among those on whom the existence tax falls.
It asks of an adequate answer that it name "the object at its own level".

The archive's Pessoa Knowledge Graph papers list Pessoa Digital among their primary-source reference archives, as a "critical digital editions project" beside the Biblioteca Nacional's Espólio and as a "digital editions project" in a list the working plan says to cite generously.

They describe it as a project that "undertakes textual encoding but remains largely internal to Portuguese academic infrastructure"; the field's pages give a founding partner at the University of Cologne, a cooperation with EAFIT University in Medellín and, for 2023, funding to integrate it into the research data infrastructure of Text+.

The edition's own address answered the census's requests of 1 November 2026, for its home page and its about page, with HTTP 418 and a challenge page stating that "the administrator of this website has set up go-away to protect the server against the scourge of AI companies aggressively scraping websites"; the census rests its row on the CCeH's page, supplied by the census's operator, and records the edition's own pages as unread.

The challenge page's footer reads "Digital Humanities at the University of Cologne" and names the Cologne Center for eHumanities, the Data Center for the Humanities and the Department for Digital Humanities.

Wikipedia has no article under the name in English or Portuguese, and an English search for "Pessoa Digital" returns no page; English Wikipedia links the edition from its Fernando Pessoa article alone and lists Project Estranhar Pessoa there as a link of its own.

The census distinguishes it from the Arquivo Pessoa, a separate resource and its neighbour among the editions of Pessoa's work, which holds the published work under its names where Pessoa Digital holds the plans and lists.

On 1 November 2026 Google's AI Overview, asked "Pessoa Digital" at a new address, gave two senses, the edition first and second João Pessoa na Palma da Mão, a municipal app of João Pessoa in Brazil and a distinct entity, from five cards: the CCeH's page, the Rostock announcement and three Instagram videos on the app, known here by their titles alone.

The Capture Registry's innocent reading is that, given a two-word name shared by a scholarly edition and a city's services, the Overview gives both senses, the edition first, and asks which the user wants.

The registry found the edition reached at the grain of its kind and its object, the plans and lists in which Pessoa assigned his works to their names, left out, and the edition's title as the Rostock card gives it, "Fernando Pessoa. Projects and Publications", uncomposed.

It found the host misassigned, the composition having "the Estranhar Pessoa project hosted by the Cologne Center for eHumanities (CCeH)" where the first card says the edition is hosted by the DCH, and the editors, named on that card, named nowhere in the composition.

The CCeH gives as a representative publication "Networks of persons and figures in Fernando Pessoa's publication plans" (2018) and refers to the edition's own pages for the list of publications. No saved source states its size, its licence or limits of its own, and how it marks the names under which Pessoa wrote, in its plans or its indexes, stays unread while its own pages refuse automated requests. The census reads the edition as keeping the place where Pessoa's authorship was planned, a record of the names' works as Pessoa assigned them before publication fixed them, and sets that record beside #940's account of distinct named authorial functions. Among the markers by which #940 tells a heteronym from a pseudonym is "A bounded corpus produced under the heteronym rather than attributed retroactively", and it holds that "A pseudonym changes the label attached to an authorial function. A heteronym changes the organization of the authorial function itself." On the census's reading the plans hold the names' works as assigned before publication, the stage of the corpus that this marker concerns. Pessoa's own typology, from his letter to Adolfo Casais Monteiro of 13 January 1935, distinguishes orthonym, heteronym and semi-heteronym, and Teresa Rita Lopes and later critics extended it with the proto-heteronym and the para-heteronym; on the archive's typology, collapsing these distinctions treats his practice as "elaborate pseudonym". English Wikipedia gives Pessoa about seventy-five names besides his own and states that he called them heteronyms, a term he invented, and it links the edition from its article on him as "Digital Edition of Fernando Pessoa", with the words "and heteronyms". The edition's network of persons and the 2018 paper on the persons and figures of the publication plans stand beside the archive's reading that Pessoa's distinctive contribution is the system of heteronyms, their reciprocal relations and the master-disciple structure. #940's counter-principle holds that "The authorial function is attributable through the civil bearer without being reducible to that bearer": the civil bearer administers, publishes and answers for the work without becoming the exhaustive source of every authorial function operating through it, and the heteronymic architecture "ensures that the collapse registers as loss". It sets "Ordinary editing, where the editor's contribution is supportive rather than function-constitutive" outside heteronymy, names "Pessoa's Caeiro, Reis, Campos, and the constellation of heteronyms around them" in the tradition it joins, and plans a deposit on the heteronymic operation in the Pessoa archive as ethical practice. The archive's essay on the meta-heteronym names a heteronymic system whose personae produce, besides literary works, the institutional apparatus, introductions, criticism, historiography and bibliography, under which those works become legible, and reads Pessoa as the first modern meta-heteronym, incompletely. It counts Sepúlveda, with Jerónimo Pizarro, Teresa Rita Lopes and Richard Zenith, in the material turn that moved Pessoa criticism from text to archive, to the trunk, the 25,000 pages, the fragments and the unexecuted projects, and holds that "Se o meta-heterônimo é uma tecnologia institucional, o arquivo é a sua materialidade". It proposes that Pessoa's infrastructure, his editorial projects among it, be read as the meta-heteronymic operation in fragmentary execution, and gives as an instance the Tábua Bibliográfica of 1928, signed by the orthonym, which lists the heteronyms' works as works of independent authors. It records the objection that most of the heteronymic prefaces stayed in the trunk, and states its own limit: the category is typological and provisional, and its validity depends on further tests in Pessoa's archive, above all in the unpublished materials of the Ficções do Interlúdio and the unexecuted editorial projects, the class of document whose plans and lists the edition holds. #1722 holds that "A heteronym is a real author's practice: Pessoa wrote as Caeiro, Reis and Campos, and nobody concludes from this that Pessoa was a character", records a heteronymic practice, Pessoa's, read as a Sybil operation, answers that a heteronym is declared, its registry published with the orthonym, the roles and the dates, and counts the heteronymous among those on whom the existence tax falls. It asks of an adequate answer that it name "the object at its own level". The archive's Pessoa Knowledge Graph papers list Pessoa Digital among their primary-source reference archives, as a "critical digital editions project" beside the Biblioteca Nacional's Espólio and as a "digital editions project" in a list the working plan says to cite generously. They describe it as a project that "undertakes textual encoding but remains largely internal to Portuguese academic infrastructure"; the field's pages give a founding partner at the University of Cologne, a cooperation with EAFIT University in Medellín and, for 2023, funding to integrate it into the research data infrastructure of Text+. loci.quote: The edition keeps the place where Pessoa's authorship was planned: the lists and plans in which he conceived his work, set beside what he published. That is a record of the names' works as Pessoa assigned them before publication fixed them, which the census reads beside #940's account of distinct named authorial functions. How it marks the names themselves stays unread until its own pages can be fetched.
A bounded corpus produced under the heteronym rather than attributed retroactively

A categoria proposta é tipológica e provisória; a sua validade depende de testes adicionais no arquivo pessoano, especialmente nos materiais inéditos das *Ficções do Interlúdio* e nos projetos editoriais inexecutados.
The *Pessoa Digital* project undertakes textual encoding but remains largely internal to Portuguese academic infrastructure.
